A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DAG, and their main text, equations, tables and figures are readable and matchable despite the changed title. However, both end with references and omit the appendices or supplementary material they cite for implementation details and additional results, limiting comparison of that promised material.

before.justification: V1 reports original PIAD benchmark results, component and feature-extractor ablations, and qualitative predictions on incomplete point clouds.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds PIAD2 results, timestep and few-shot experiments, and qualitative diffusion-model analyses.

M1.justification: The main frozen diffusion/point-encoder pipeline, decoder and losses remain. V1 describes a trainable self-prompt captioner; v2 describes an Affordance Semantics Encoder with projected, weighted late-layer CLIP features, but still calls it self-prompt in Section 4.4. The descriptions and missing supplements leave unclear whether this changes the component or expands its documentation.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates PIAD seen/unseen settings and partial 3D AffordanceNet clouds. V2 retains these, renaming the original benchmark PIAD1, and adds PIAD2 with separate seen, unseen-object and unseen-affordance evaluations in Table 2. This substantially broadens evaluated generalization coverage.

E2.justification: V2 removes OpenAD and LMAffordance3D from the corresponding original-benchmark Table 1, retaining the other seven baselines. FRCNN appears in the new PIAD2 comparison, and Figure 2 adds CLIP and DINO to the qualitative attention comparison.

E3.justification: V2 introduces training with 1, 3 or 5 labeled examples per affordance category, compared against full-data PFU and IAGNet, plus a controlled timestep comparison at t=0, 50 and 100. Original metrics and the stated 80-epoch main training budget remain. The few-shot test split and sampling procedure are not specified.

E4.justification: V2 retains the component, captioner and backbone ablations while adding timestep sensitivity, few-shot data-efficiency analysis, attention comparisons and incorrect-HOI-instruction case studies. Its partial-cloud visualization also expands from four to eight examples. These additions test several questions absent from v1.

E5.justification: Both versions report selected DAG results with ± values without defining the statistic or disclosing run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. V2 adds no identifiable statistical estimation procedure; changes to individual uncertainty values concern results.

E6.justification: V2 adds PIAD2 mIoUs of 47.19, 28.93 and 16.09 across its three settings, plus timestep results and 1/3/5-shot mIoUs of 12.98/14.34/15.74. Retained main-result means match, but Table 1's unseen AUC changes from 76.69±0.7 to 76.69±0.3. The seen CLS-only ablation MAE changes from 0.176 to 0.116 in v1 Table 2 versus v2 Table 4.

T1.justification: Equation 2 corrects the formally specified U-Net input from the noise-schedule coefficient to the noisy image x_t and uses image-derived conditioning, aligning the equation with the captioner description. There are no new theorems or proofs; the remaining mathematical changes mainly clarify notation.

C1.justification: The central claims about transferring diffusion-model affordance knowledge and outperforming grounding baselines remain. V2's abstract explicitly extends the generalization claim to the challenging one-shot setting. Its first-diffusion-framework claim was already present in v1's related-work discussion.

C2.justification: V2 removes v1's explicit main limitation that DAG requires substantial 3D training data and interprets few-shot results as strong novel-category generalization. It also interprets incorrect-instruction examples as evidence of genuine interaction understanding and attributes timestep degradation to noise impairing texture and spatial localization. These materially change applicability and mechanism interpretations.

D1.justification: V2 documents late-layer CLIP projections and weighted feature aggregation. Its abstract replaces the project-page pointer with an explicit code-release statement and repository address, whose availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. The stated hardware, optimizer, learning rate and main training duration remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 substantially broadens cited coverage of diffusion-affordance and MLLM research, adding works including Beyond the Contact, DAVID, Affordance Diffusion, H2OFlow and VideoAfford. Section 2.1 expands discussion of OpenAD, LMAffordance and SeqAfford, while the self-prompt reference is removed. The central novelty positioning remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and substantial related-work passages are rewritten, with additional editing throughout the method. V2 changes the title, author information and component terminology, creates a dedicated open-world-analysis subsection, and replaces Conclusion and Limitation with Conclusion and Future Work.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document from two columns to one, redraws the motivation and pipeline diagrams, and consolidates v1 Figures 3–5 into Figure 3. It expands Figure 2 and the partial-cloud visualization and adds three tables. Existing qualitative comparisons and ablations are also relocated and reformatted.

improvement.justification: PIAD2's separate unseen-affordance evaluation and the controlled timestep ablation provide useful new checks of generalization and design choices. These gains are tempered by removed baseline comparisons and weaker qualification: Section 4.5 overstates Table 7, where few-shot DAG beats full-data PFU but remains below full-data IAGNet, while v1's explicit data-requirement limitation disappears. The net improvement is therefore limited.
